informationlinked is the agreement of description, acceptance, and support within a fixed scope. A typed basic function that selects a content description at stage 0. It does not provide truth determination, default values for unknown conditions, interpretation of natural language, or polymorphic selection of arbitrary types.

entries.name: closeddiscourse

context: discourse: an update that passes the reference state and situation to subsequent checks. Updates by constructors are monotonic with respect to subsequent operations and preserve the situation.

Scope and position are to be specified. Candidates for natural language pronouns and accessibility are not to be automatically inferred.
General higher-order functions are not to be certified as monotonic and situation-preserving solely based on their update type. Interpret updates constructed from the constructors here.

Conditional statements are to be read as checking all successful states of the antecedent with the consequent. Readings that carry out the introduction of options outward or that involve counterfactuals require separate constructions.
Basis for identification is not to be automatically proven. Unknown inputs are to be rejected in evaluation and are not to be converted into absence of candidates or negation.

context: owners: a finite sequence of characters corresponding to the description sequence and position.

contrast: The state is a set of finite pairs of characters and utterance descriptions adopted in conversation. Do not automatically certify psychological belief, truth of content, or legal obligation. Records also include negative content and mutually contradictory content.

If the lengths of the two sequences differ, the state is invalid. Rearranging one side alone changes the combination of character and description. Duplication of the same pair and the order of pairs do not constitute a difference in state. The number of events and their temporal order are represented in a separate history.

Acceptance permits existing records of the same description; new additions separately require prior absence; withdrawal is read as excluding previously existing records, and correction is read as a change to a syntactically different description.

The certification relationship of withdrawal and correction is a new explicit interpretation input and must not be confused with an input that does not increase the number of primitive declarations; do not infer events or reasons from mere state differences.

Adopted descriptions are utterances at stage 0; the construction of descriptions by function application is performed as quotations, and upon acceptance only the target description is evaluated; if the target cannot be identified, rejection occurs; this is not automatic extension to arbitrary-stage quotations or types.

Update is a definition that inspects the relationship between before and after states and is not a command that automatically rewrites the state of external applications; history examples separately retain the old state, each action, the basis, and the point in time, and linkage alone does not supplement the validity of individual updates.

Description matching is syntactic matching; do not infer synonymy of different syntaxes or pragmatic acceptance; do not convert unknown inputs into negation but evaluate as rejection; finite models are not all real conversations or proofs of infinite domains.

contrast: Definitions reuse the bodies and meanings of existing speech-principals. No new primitive declarations are introduced; remaining interpersonal and normative relations are passed as arguments that explicitly specify type and interpretation.

Advice, promises, and commands of the request/reason-presentation type are explicit constructions of reading and are not automatically classified from surface form. Each profile is neither exclusive nor exhaustive.
The grounds for applying targets/solicits/supports/undertakes/claims are interpretation inputs. It is not claimed that these social and volitional relations are reduced to logical operations alone.

Presentation, receipt, understanding, acceptance, refusal, and realization are distinguished. Acceptance and refusal are not merely negations of each other; non-response and contradictory records can also be described.

In request, the actor is fixed as the recipient; in promise, the actor is fixed as the speaker. The truth of quoted actions or utterances is not evaluated by profile judgment; explicit de-quotation is performed only when realization is questioned.

Exercise of authority indication and authority legitimacy, acceptance and valid obligation, suitability evaluation for a purpose and purpose achievement are distinguished. Deadline, termination, non-performance judgment, partial answer, and conversation update are separately connected.

Indirect requests can link the description of the surface question with the requested action via targets, but this is not a mechanism for automatic inference of that linkage. Unknown inputs are not replaced with false or unaccepted.
Circular character connection, application to other domains, and learning/third-party reading are continuing challenges.

Acceptance permits existing records of the same description; new additions separately require prior absence; withdrawal is read as excluding previously existing records, and correction is read as a change to a syntactically different description.

The certification relationship of withdrawal and correction is a new explicit interpretation input and must not be confused with an input that does not increase the number of primitive declarations; do not infer events or reasons from mere state differences.

contrast: Distinguish assertion, background, attribution, selection of subject/comparison, and actual truth. Do not provide all usages of natural language only/also/even/but, nor automatic identification of discourse topics.

Even if content is unknown, reception records can be retained as quotations. Acceptance, implication, and information comparison requiring content evaluation reject unknown inputs. Logical operations do not short-circuit.

Retain one description constructed as input and do not generate new descriptions or unverified descriptions of external origin.

contrast: Generic statements based on typical examples share the explicit reading of existing r2be/r2bf/r2bg/r2fa. They are not the only meaning of all generic statements, nor do they represent universal quantification or majority rule of current instances.

Valid decision domains are mutually exclusive, but empty or universal sets are permitted. In invalid scales or overlapping domains, each judgment becomes false, distinguishing failure of validity from negation of the object.

Distinguish satisfying an upward-closed goal criterion from actually achieving the goal. The six definitions of the modality scale with both ends retain the old text and do not force both ends on general degrees.

Distinguish glyph reference, registered semantics, context-specific candidates, enumeration completion, selection, and content evaluation. Do not collapse candidates into the logical disjunction of content, and do not fill unverified with false.

A meaning function is a type that constructs content from a finite sequence of individual arguments, handling 0-argument propositions, 1-argument properties, and multi-argument relations with the same construction. It is not a newly created polymorphic function of arbitrary type. For other types, use the existing typed quotation application.

Reference to a glyph form and reference to a semantic role are interpretation inputs; assigning an identifier does not mean the semantics are defined. In examples, relationships such as the meaning body and selection are constructed in Native.

Checking item consistency and term count does not guarantee the totality of the meaning function. Logical operations are not short-circuited; passing invalid arguments to a partial meaning function may cause evaluation to be rejected. Confirm the term count first, then separate meaning application from truth evaluation.

positive: The scope of candidates affirmed as the answer. In the case of two objects, it is an ordered pair and is not substituted by two surrounding sets.
negative: The scope of candidates explicitly stated as not being the answer. Do not automatically set the complement of the affirmative domain.
closed: An explicit statement that the affirmed candidates are all the answers. This is a separate truth input from whether it is actually exhaustive.
contrast: The type to be published is the question of an individual and the question of two individuals. Existing question/answer_matches handle an arbitrary finite number and type, but this extension to the inspection of these two types does not generalize to proofs for all types. Identical constructions for other types are performed as explicit typed definitions.

The question and the domain of affirmation/negation are fixed in the explicitly stated context. Do not infer the scope of answers or the intent of exhaustiveness from natural language. Distinguish correctness from what is actually presented and accepted.

partial is correct non-empty information that does not explicitly state exhaustiveness and does not mean that it is actually insufficient. complete is verified by explicit checking of all answers; covers alone does not constitute the utterance of all answers.

unsettled is a known candidate outside the explicit information. Unknown interpretations are evaluation rejections and are not converted to negation or falsity of unanswered. informative does not measure new information quantity or utility.

The projection of two objects universally quantifies the counterpart. The correspondence is not restored from the candidate sets of first and second alone. Questions to fixed objects preserve the correspondence of the original pair.

A finite model is not an evaluator of infinite domains. Do not substitute total answers in infinite domains such as numbers with finite samples. The truth of quoted answer content and the presentation, acceptance, correction, and withdrawal of the answer as such are separate conditions. Updates to the conversation state are subsequent tasks.

entries.name: permissionconflict
entries.meaning: A coexistence of an active permission of a specified polarity and a requirement for the opposite polarity.
context: source: the source of the requirement or permission, fixed within the same normative system or institution.
person: the person who is the target.
role: the stance of the person to which the norm applies.
activity: The same activity whose performance or nonperformance is at issue.
description: a closed description of a Noema function that creates content from the person and activity. Do not substitute with sentences of the source language or truth values of the situation.
polarity: a norm where true means the description holds and false means it does not hold.
context: the situation in which the norm and fulfillment are evaluated.
required: a requirement for the same seven items. The norm that certifies the requirement and the interpretation must be specified separately.
allowed: positive permission for the same seven items. Do not supplement from the absence of requirement/prohibition or physical possibility.
contrast: Explicitly specify the convention for inputting adoption, application, and basis of requirements, permissions, and norms. The definition body alone does not determine social legitimacy or priority of exceptions.
The range of comparison candidates and priority relations are inputs of the specified reading. Do not turn the absence of a best candidate or premise impossibility into empty success.
Unknown relations reject evaluation. Do not convert to empty candidates, absence of norms, or negation.
Execute the action description only when evaluating fulfillment. Do not automatically conflate permission and ability, norm and fact, counterfactual and causality.

The contrast between finite models and two subjects is not a meaning of all natural languages or a proof of infinite domains. Separate registration of circle characters and third-party interpretation is required.

entries.name: positivescales
entries.meaning: Three rational unit scales are all positive.
context: firstscale: the first positive scale.
secondscale: the second positive scale.
thirdscale: the third positive scale.
contrast: amountat is the magnitude of a non-negative rational quantity. Do not translate into error intervals, arbitrary real values, irrational scales, origin shifts, or universal conversions in logarithmic units. Preserve the old real-number version and coordinate definitions.
Registration in the circle character shared dictionary, learning documents, and third-party reading are incomplete.
Do not derive quantity from the number of containers or parts. Fix the overall range and measurement situation. Reject evaluation of unknown inputs.

Reuse the four primitive declarations for existing rational number comparison, addition, additive inverse, and multiplication. Since the type of a function alone cannot force the interpretation of standard arithmetic, preserve the meaning conventions.

Preserve the thirteen definitions for existing dimension, kind, and scale. Add ten definitions for new measurement and content. The three definitions for multiple modules are shared with the same body.

Do not automatically certify the basis for reality of registration, measurement, parts, overlap, and completeness. amountsum also requires the equation of addition and does not infer that any quantity is always additive.

right: the right pair of an ordered conjunction.

entries.name: speechtargeted
entries.meaning: Connects an explicit interpretation that treats the same presentation and its same action/target/speech description as the object sought by the specified actor's action description.
context: person: the presenter of the same utterance.
activity: the act connecting the occurrence, presentation, and receipt of the same utterance.
recipient: one recipient who actually presents.
subject: the target to which the utterance template is applied; do not equate with the actor without authorization.
message: a description of a closed function that creates an utterance value from the target; use description identity and do not evaluate the content.
context: the situation in which the same utterance act is evaluated.
occurs: the occurrence relationship between act and situation.
presents: the presenter-side participation relationship of presenter, act, and situation.
conveys: the presentational relation of act, recipient, object, description, and situation.
actor: the subject of the sought action.
action: a description of a closed action function that creates the proposition content from the subject; may be a planned action, and is not executed upon quotation.
targets: the interpretive bindings of action/target/surface speech description/actor/action description/situation. Do not infer the request solely from the form of the question.
contrast: Definitions reuse the bodies and meanings of existing speech-principals. No new primitive declarations are introduced; remaining interpersonal and normative relations are passed as arguments that explicitly specify type and interpretation.

Advice, promises, and commands of the request/reason-presentation type are explicit constructions of reading and are not automatically classified from surface form. Each profile is neither exclusive nor exhaustive.
The grounds for applying targets/solicits/supports/undertakes/claims are interpretation inputs. It is not claimed that these social and volitional relations are reduced to logical operations alone.

Presentation, receipt, understanding, acceptance, refusal, and realization are distinguished. Acceptance and refusal are not merely negations of each other; non-response and contradictory records can also be described.

In request, the actor is fixed as the recipient; in promise, the actor is fixed as the speaker. The truth of quoted actions or utterances is not evaluated by profile judgment; explicit de-quotation is performed only when realization is questioned.

Exercise of authority indication and authority legitimacy, acceptance and valid obligation, suitability evaluation for a purpose and purpose achievement are distinguished. Deadline, termination, non-performance judgment, partial answer, and conversation update are separately connected.

Indirect requests can link the description of the surface question with the requested action via targets, but this is not a mechanism for automatic inference of that linkage. Unknown inputs are not replaced with false or unaccepted.
Circular character connection, application to other domains, and learning/third-party reading are continuing challenges.

entries.meaning: When a promise of the same speaker and action description is presented, and the presentation situation coincides with the starting point of a deadline condition, and there is a requirement for that constructed deadline condition at that starting point. Do not infer the validity of the requirement from the promise alone.

source: the source of the institution, norm, or stance issuing the requirement.
role: The role of the person who is the target of the requirement.
performancedescription: a closed individual description of the required target activity.
historydescription: a closed description of the history range.
orderdescription: a closed description of the temporal order.
issueddescription: a closed description of the starting point.
duedescription: a closed description of the deadline.
assessment: the time point at which the state is evaluated.
required: A requirement concerning the same source, person, role, activity, description, polarity, and situation; it retains the record of the starting point.
contrast: A positive deadline requirement is satisfied if it holds at least once between a single start point and the deadline; the reading includes the deadline but excludes the start point; it does not automatically include full fulfillment of sustained obligations, repetition, multiple clauses, retroactive exemption, or revalidation.

Release at the deadline time is treated as within the deadline; release after the deadline does not erase non-fulfillment at the deadline time, even if it has been released up to the present; this explicitly stated convention is not treated as a rule common to all systems.

The fact that a request existed at the start point is not a universal proof of the norm's legitimacy; the same basis can be constructed with existing groundedrule/normwitness; authority to release and the act of release are additional explicit interpretation inputs.

fulfilled, released, breached, and late are not mutually exclusive state names; late realization or release after the deadline can coexist with past non-fulfillment at the deadline; unless explicit indication of investigation completion is given, the negative conditions for pending/breached/late are not treated as holding.

The norm description of the request target is constructed by applying the same closed argument description to the quoted deadlineclause; it is not substituted for descriptions of other acts, activities, or time points that happen to have the same truth value.

A time history can be described as a frame including future evaluation points, but this is distinct from observation completion; a finite evaluator does not short-circuit logical operations, so if the interpretation required for execution is unknown for time points outside the condition, it rejects; unknown is not converted to unrealized.

Finite models and single-frame binding diagnosis do not prove certification grounds for continuous time universals or actual promises/institutions; withdrawal of conversation adoption records alone does not compensate for release of a request.

entries.name: proofancestors
entries.meaning: Along a finite order, construct as a relation each item itself and the ancestors of premises constructed previously; rejection of cycles or out-of-order sequences is performed separately via proofverified.
context: order: a finite sequence of evidence records arranged from premise to conclusion for certification. Not a sequence of timestamps.
parents: the relation of child records and direct premise records. Requires a convention to provide all related premises.
contrast: A reading of belief composed from candidate situations and recognized descriptions. This is not a theory that explains all uses, understanding, memory, rationality, or logical omniscience of human belief. It distinguishes recognition from actual truth.

Observation, transmission, availability, inference, recording, candidates, recognition, and origin are explicit interpretation inputs. Do not confuse the addition of primitive declarations with the reduction of all these social meanings.

A finite evidence-dependent sequence is a structural condition for local certification and specified all premises. It is not a logical proof that guarantees content truth or evidence reliability. It can connect evidenceentails with the same premise description as evidenceinferred in local inference.

Use of premises, description sequences, logical implication, and actual truth of premises are distinct. Inference from empty premises can be made explicit, but if the source set is empty, it is not certified as support from a different origin.

Rehearsal from the same origin is kept as an element of the root set. Do not treat the non-empty and non-intersecting root set as probabilistic independence, absence of common cause, or increase in truth or confidence. Identification of origin and exhaustiveness are interpretation conventions.

Make candidate scope and comparison scope explicit. Do not elevate finite inspection to equivalence or validity over all possible situations. Do not treat beliefgroundedtrue as a sufficient condition for general knowledge.
Unknown interpretations reject execution. Since logical operations do not short-circuit, if necessary inputs are unknown even inside conditions that ultimately become false, reject them.

A certification sequence is a finite dependent order within one context and does not automatically include record occurrence time or causal order. History updates that overwrite past records by changing input relations later are constructed separately.

contrast: Definitions reuse the bodies and meanings of existing speech-principals. No new primitive declarations are introduced; remaining interpersonal and normative relations are passed as arguments that explicitly specify type and interpretation.

Advice, promises, and commands of the request/reason-presentation type are explicit constructions of reading and are not automatically classified from surface form. Each profile is neither exclusive nor exhaustive.
The grounds for applying targets/solicits/supports/undertakes/claims are interpretation inputs. It is not claimed that these social and volitional relations are reduced to logical operations alone.

Presentation, receipt, understanding, acceptance, refusal, and realization are distinguished. Acceptance and refusal are not merely negations of each other; non-response and contradictory records can also be described.

In request, the actor is fixed as the recipient; in promise, the actor is fixed as the speaker. The truth of quoted actions or utterances is not evaluated by profile judgment; explicit de-quotation is performed only when realization is questioned.

Exercise of authority indication and authority legitimacy, acceptance and valid obligation, suitability evaluation for a purpose and purpose achievement are distinguished. Deadline, termination, non-performance judgment, partial answer, and conversation update are separately connected.

Indirect requests can link the description of the surface question with the requested action via targets, but this is not a mechanism for automatic inference of that linkage. Unknown inputs are not replaced with false or unaccepted.
Circular character connection, application to other domains, and learning/third-party reading are continuing challenges.

Presentation, receipt, understanding, acceptance, refusal, and realization are distinguished. Acceptance and refusal are not merely negations of each other; non-response and contradictory records can also be described.

Circular character connection, application to other domains, and learning/third-party reading are continuing challenges.

entries.meaning: Treat as a rigid object with fixed shape under specified settings. This is an idealization commonly applied to the material axis and the ruler, and does not include the law that length is equal during acceleration or in all systems.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: perpendicularmaterialaxes
entries.meaning: The directions of two material axes are orthogonal. This is a meaning convention that the inner product of local Euclidean directions is zero. The connection to actual directions and physical measurement is incomplete.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: parallelmaterialaxes
entries.meaning: Two material axes are geometrically parallel. This relation does not exclude the opposite direction by itself. Coincidence of position is not required.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: coincidentsupportinglines
entries.meaning: The geometric supporting lines of two material axes coincide. This is a condition stronger than mere parallelism, not the identity of the object.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: actsforpriorintention
entries.meaning: A teleological relation where an action is performed as a means to pursue the same goal already stated by the agent in the intention location within the scope. The intention refers to the location of the statement of intention, while the object and content of the intention are specified by another relation. Do not replace the novel occurrence of the feeling of intending the goal with the achievement of the goal, the sufficiency and success of the means, or the proof of objective causal relations. Maintain the identity between the execution of the action and the intention on the synthetic side.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: adoptsquantitydesignation
entries.meaning: A naming declaration where the author, at a node, adopts a designation that calls the quantity of the same document as a symbol according to the convention of a closed rule for objects, real values, and situations. Distinguish this from mere reference to previously written notation, while preserving the rule's object, unit of measurement, and role. Do not derive physical truth from the literal form of the symbol, nor require performing measurement by executing the rule here, or others' consent or the first naming in history.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: studiesdirectedrepresentationchange
entries.meaning: An inquiry that takes as its research subject the rule for transferring from the first representation to the second representation, along with its conditions and theoretical explanation/derivation, while maintaining the respective representation systems for the first value expression and the second value expression bound to the same object by a closed correspondence relation. The arguments of the relation are, in order: first expression, second expression, first representation system, second representation system, and situation. Specify object identity, quantity, scale, and qualified representation system by citing the corresponding relation. While handling transformation rules rather than mere name changes or a list of two expressions, the presentation of this subject itself does not derive that the rule is discovered, proven, total, reversible, linear, or that a particular formula is correct.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: spacetimecoordinatetuple
entries.meaning: A set of coordinate values having three position components and one time component. The combination of values with each system, unit, and event is required by shc.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: coordinatetuplecomponent
entries.meaning: Extract the real cut of a specified component from a set of coordinate values. Handle the three position components with the common length unit ta and the time component with the common time unit rb. Do not use values in arguments other than the role.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: asksphysicalfunctionmeaning
entries.meaning: Present as a question the physical meaning of a function specified by the author. Distinguish this from a calculation problem asking for values.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: selectscharacterizedobjectforconsideration
entries.meaning: A discursive act where the author takes an object, specified in characterization, into the scope of consideration at a node and directs attention to that object. The description specifies features and settings of the same object, and the synthetic side maintains identical reference with the object. Do not imply visual witnessing, cutting of material, execution of experiments, the truth of the description content, or the achievement of the purpose of consideration. This is a presentation relation distinct from the adoption of hypotheses or assertion of results.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: describedindividualfunctionreference
entries.meaning: A reference to a function from individual to individual that is checked for correspondence by binding to a description of a closed role relation, within the same document, location, and presented context. The role is defined in the text. Do not derive the holding of the role, proof of existence, or uniqueness from the acquisition of the reference, nor execute the cited role or candidate function. Reject unknown references and do not select any mapping that fits the role or fill in values.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: attributesphysicalfunctioninterpretation
entries.meaning: The author gives the physical interpretation of a function by specified measurement content. Distinguish this from calculated facts of function values or proof at all speeds.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: attributesspatialsymmetryreason
entries.meaning: The author presents the content of the conclusion within the scope, citing as a physical symmetry the fact that the author does not treat specially the change of orientation of spatial arrangement under the same background and scale, given that the author is a node. What remains invariant in terms of which object, arrangement, change, and range of quantity is made explicit in the composed content of the conclusion. This is an attribution in the discourse indicating the type of reason, and it does not imply the experimental verification of that symmetry, theorems of all physical laws, or the automatic proof or obviousness of the conclusion itself.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: describedsituationcutfunctionreference
entries.meaning: A reference to a function that returns a cut for each situation, linked to a closed description of role relations within the same document, section, and presentation context. Roles are defined in the text. Retrieval of the reference does not derive the holding, existence, or uniqueness of the role, nor does it execute the quoted role or candidate function. Unknown references are rejected; no candidate is selected arbitrarily and no value is interpolated.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: transverselighttrialscope
entries.meaning: The entire trial range of light round trips considered under the specified horizontal axis direction and setting. This is not limited to observed samples but includes ideal trials.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: trialtransversedistancecandidate
entries.meaning: Candidates for the positive one-way distance of the same horizontal direction trial. Connection to coordinate difference and both propagation times is required by slp.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: trialtransversespeedcandidate
entries.meaning: Candidates for the horizontal component velocity of the same trial. Distinguished from the total speed V, it connects to the sum of squares, square root, and propagation time.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: completetransversetrialscope
entries.meaning: An explicit premise that the trial ranges of the y and z directions of zej exhaust the subject of discussion. This is not certification by finite inspection.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: analogousearlierargument
entries.meaning: The author positions this section as an argument similar to a specified preceding argumentation. This does not mean mechanical equivalence or already derived results.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: movingtestforceresponse
entries.meaning: response is the ideal local mechanical-force response when a signed test quantity of kind, measured in amountunit, is assigned the specified coordinate-time velocity at that point, using the calibrated right-handed orthogonal axes and lengthunit/timeunit of the same frame and the external electric/magnetic fields in the same context and region. The arguments are four coordinates, a signed quantity, and three velocity components; the result has three components in the same axes and forceunit. This extends the existing stationary-test convention to a function that also takes velocity: the test quantity and size approach zero to remove their effect on the configuration, and the response is normalized per unit quantity. Different velocities are hypothetical comparisons against the same background; they do not mean that incompatible velocities are simultaneously realized at the same event. Force is identified through its contribution to momentum change or a mechanical action balancing it. This concerns the contribution of these two fields, not a resultant including gravity, support forces, or other forces. Physical attribution is not inferred from numerical values. Actual measurement, actual existence of finite test bodies, and any particular force law are not implied. Agreement with the electric-side response at zero velocity, decomposition of contributions, velocity dependence, cross products, and approximation order are composed separately.
context: Maintains the same object, event, system, unit, background, both fields, and presentation context.
Composes as a separate relation: velocity response, quotation of terminology, old and new ways of speaking, and physical coordinate correspondence.

entries.name: quotedvectorquantityterm
entries.meaning: Used as a term that quotes expression in the same document's wording and picks it up, interpreting the role of the vector quantity it points to according to a closed rule in the same situation. The rule takes as arguments three-component values and situation, binding object, system, unit, and physical role within the rule. The quotation here serves the function of picking up terminology and does not automatically add reproduction of others' utterances, irony, or negation of propositions. Substitution of meaning by spelling alone, execution of quoted content, or the holding of the rule and its automatic proof of physical laws is not implied.
context: Maintains the same object, event, system, unit, background, both fields, and presentation context.
Composes as a separate relation: velocity response, quotation of terminology, old and new ways of speaking, and physical coordinate correspondence.

entries.name: establishednewwordingcontrast
entries.meaning: Regarding two ways of describing within the same scope, established is the way of speaking already used in that discussion, and new is the way of speaking newly presented in this discussion, set in opposition. This distinguishes from mere temporal order of utterance or truth value/superiority of one side; it does not imply prohibition or complete abandonment of the former, that the latter is the first in history, or that the two are unconditionally strictly equivalent.
context: Maintains the same object, event, system, unit, background, both fields, and presentation context.
Composes as a separate relation: velocity response, quotation of terminology, old and new ways of speaking, and physical coordinate correspondence.

entries.name: physicalcoordinatecorrespondence
entries.meaning: A correspondence convention linking descriptions of two physical coordinate systems, first and second, within the same context, via a mapping that re-expresses the coordinates of the same event. The origins, axis orientations and scales, and calibration, synchronization, and time origin of local clocks of both systems are fixed. Input is the four coordinates of the first system, output is the four coordinates of the second system. The same convention is applied across the entire domain of that coordinate description, not only at points with measurement records, including coordinates of unoccupied places. Values are represented in lengthunit/timeunit, but simultaneity in different systems or agreement of numerical times is not implied. This is a relation attributing which numerical function realizes this correspondence to the physical setting of axes and clocks, not certified by arbitrary numerical mappings alone. Specific transformation formulas, relative velocity, rest of the object, and laws of fields and forces are not included and are separately composed. Experiment execution or the existence of objects at all real number points is not required.
context: Maintains the same object, event, system, unit, background, both fields, and presentation context.
Composes as a separate relation: velocity response, quotation of terminology, old and new ways of speaking, and physical coordinate correspondence.

entries.name: segmentrecord
entries.meaning: Each reference to a segment is a record of a single interval that follows the propagation of the same ray emitted from the specified object emitter via emission, within the same system, units, and context. The start is an event of emission or a subsequent event on the same propagation, and the end is an event thereafter. The emitter is an emitting object possessing the same material portion and state of motion, and must not be confused with a ray or a local clock. The target is not limited solely to the emitter's rest, uniform velocity, or specific velocity. To preserve values per interval, the record individual includes the system, units, and settings, and does not unconditionally assign values from different systems into the same record. Conditions such as actual instrument installation or having been observed are not required; hypothetical propagation settings are also handled.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: lawbranch
entries.meaning: In the specified physical law system theory, a law belongs to the laws concerning the phenomena of a branch. The same law is a single general relation sharing conventions of physical quantities, application conditions, and units, and is not merely another formula with the same name. It is not a condition that selects only the laws that hold afterward, but rather a classification of all laws handled by the system. Fields may overlap; one does not make electromechanics and optics mutually exclusive lists of laws.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: electrodynamics
entries.meaning: A reference to the field of electromechanics. Like eie5, it treats as laws the phenomena of charge and current, the fields on the electrical side and the magnetic side, and their generation, change, and action on matter. This is distinct from a reference to a specific Maxwell theory or the usual understanding of that time.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: optics
entries.meaning: A reference to the field of optics. It treats as laws physical phenomena and their relations caused by light, such as emission, propagation, direction and velocity, reflection and refraction, and interference. Here, light is not identified with a specific particle model or a material transmission medium, and overlap with electromechanics is not excluded.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: fieldlawcompleteness
entries.meaning: Regarding this point of theory, eisbe exhausts the object laws of electromechanics and optics, eisbj exhausts all physical history candidates for comparison of their admissibility and inadmissibility, and vh exhausts all corresponding descriptions in each eligible coordinate system, constituting completeness of scope. Laws possess content of physical quantities and their relations; vi is their conformity to that content, and eisbi evaluates their holding as laws of the same content. It does not admit selecting only observed examples, conforming histories, matching systems, or self-evident laws. It does not infer completeness from a finite test sample, but reads as a universal physical range input.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: lawgovernsframe
entries.meaning: When the physical quantities and application conditions of the same law are interpreted in a specified coordinate system, the law holds as a general relation governing the phenomena it targets. This is not that any virtual history conforms to the law, but that it states the holding as a law. It is distinguished from conformity to description candidates vi or preservation of conformity across different systems. Mere identity of the law's string does not constitute holding, and it does not truly complete unknown physical inputs.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: fieldhistory
entries.meaning: Physical candidate histories of states and changes of objects, charges, currents, electromagnetic fields, light, etc., for comparing the admissibility and inadmissibility of laws in this point. They possess description conditions such as identity of target and quantity, range of space and time, and initial conditions, and vh expresses the same history with quantities and coordinates of each system. It is not limited to histories that actually existed or to histories that conform to the compared laws. It distinguishes physical descriptibility as a candidate and conformity to laws. The necessary full candidate range is required by eisbh.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: absoluterest
entries.meaning: A reference to the concept of absolute rest. This is a rest that is privilegedly determined regardless of which coordinate system or other object is chosen, and is distinguished from position invariance eiah relative to a certain reference system. The very act of describing this concept does not assert the physical existence of such rest, space, or medium.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: newtonianmechanics
entries.meaning: A reference to the field of mechanics. It handles the relations of mechanical actions and state changes such as motion of objects, mass, force, and momentum. Here, it refers to the same Newtonian mechanics as eisbd, and does not reduce the claims in electromechanics and optics to problems of mechanical action alone.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: conceptproperty
entries.meaning: In phenomena of a specified field, a property corresponds to a physical characteristic of a concept. Regarding absolute rest, it points to the difference that the privileged rest is characterized on the side of physical phenomena, not merely a descriptive difference of position being constant in a chosen coordinate. It does not treat differences of only name, coordinate values, or explanation format, or mere unobservation, as corresponding characteristics. The negation of this relation is not replaced with the non-existence of the object, motion, or relative rest itself.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: geometricpath
entries.meaning: The attribution of a geometric quantity as length, measured in length units calibrated in a specified system, to the spatial path length traversed by the same ray through the same interval. Adopt the arc length as the supremum of the lengths of all finite broken lines obtained by sequentially subdividing the path, and connect it to a material length scale identical to that of the spatial metric of the reference system. Do not substitute the distance between endpoints for the length of a curved path, and distinguish it from the optical length of a medium multiplied by its refractive index. Require the identity, continuity, and existence of the path's length as physical inputs, and do not infer values from unknown trajectories. This does not mean implementing a general calculation of the upper limit of broken lines anew here.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: calibratedunits
entries.meaning: A calibration convention for units that compares the length of space in a specified system with a stationary standard scale and reads time using a common scale of ideal clocks of eisb7. The specified velocity unit is the unit obtained by dividing this length unit by the time unit, requiring no additional conversion factor to a quotient of numbers. Use the same physical unit conventions in each system, and do not identify units solely based on matching coordinate names. Do not mix scales of length and time, and do not supplement the original text with specific SI units or numerical values.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: lightsegmentrange
entries.meaning: Candidates for intervals of light propagation in a vacuum, described in a specified system, units, and context, that belong to the scope of application of this law. The scope includes hypothetical settings that vary the motion state of the emission source, the emission location, the direction, the time, and all partial intervals. Do not select only records where the velocity equals a desired value, and do not restrict the scope to observed lists or stationary light sources. The physical attribution, validity of reading, and velocity relationships of each record are verified under separate conditions.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: lightsegmentcompleteness
entries.meaning: The completeness of the scope in which eiscd exhausts all light rays, all directions, all times, all non-zero partial intervals required by this law, and all settings that vary the motion state of the emission source. Two samples with a fixed light source state are insufficient, and excerpts containing only candidates with matching results are not permitted. Completeness is not certified from finite inspections or unit names.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: designatescontent
entries.meaning: When the designation is used with the term 'designation' within a specified text scope, the naming convention holds that the designation refers to the same content specified by a closed target. Distinguish this from similarity in spelling, the fact that the object happens to have the same truth value, or the verification of that content. The designation is used as an abbreviation for the target content, and no definitions unrelated to that content are added. The position of the scope and the tense in the original text are specified separately.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: followingscope
entries.meaning: Refers to the entire text following the portion 'after' within the same document that has the same scope. This is the subsequent scope based on the order of the document, and is distinguished from referring only to the current sentence, past portions, physical future times, or specific subsequent portions. This is used when evaluating a textual foreshadowing that this will be called by this name from now on, without requiring that all subsequent sentences necessarily use that term.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: numberedheading
entries.meaning: A node is a numbered heading that opens a division of a document, and a division directly belongs to a parent within the same document hierarchy. Level is a positive integer hierarchy depth counted with the document at depth 0, and ordinal is a positive integer section or chapter number displayed on the page. In this treatise, depth 1 refers to a part and depth 2 refers to a section. Do not simply replace the ordinal with a position in an array, and allow section numbers to continue across parts. The scope of control of a division extends from this heading to immediately before the next heading of the same depth or a higher-level heading, including lower-level headings and their text. Distinguish the section indicated by a heading from the location of the heading, and do not create physical quantities from the font or glyph of numbers.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: headingtopic
entries.meaning: The heading of a node indicates to the reader the subject of the discourse to be treated from now on in the same division, as a closed topic research area. This is guidance for the entire section, and does not mean that each sentence repeats the topic name, that all fields are covered, that the truth of the physical claims in the text is established, or that definitions and derivations are completed. Citations of the topic are used to identify the subject and do not execute specific physical examples on the spot.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: anticipatesdefinition
entries.meaning: The author, at a node, foreshadows to the reader that the principle content identified as the target will be formulated and defined in a subsequent portion of the same document, named 'definition', in the following manner. This is a forward reference to the immediate definition, and is distinguished from merely using a term later, defining different content, or reviewing past definitions. The order of the reference target is specified compositionally, and this foreshadowing does not lead to the completion of formulation, the truth of the content, or verification.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: framecomparison
entries.meaning: A description convention for assigning time to the spatial arrangement of first, expressed with an origin and three mutually orthogonal axes yn/yo/yp that are normal to each other, and a stationary length scale, for the same physical coordinate system first and second; the clock synchronization, common reference, and calibration of clocks at rest in that system assign the time. lengthunit and timeunit are those scales. The positions of second's origin, axes, grid, and instrument installation are described using the same first coordinates and time, without mixing simple axis nameplates or clock readings from another system. The range of all placement points and all time points of the second system, the existence of values, and the type of motion are separately required.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: fixedconfigurationpoint
entries.meaning: The full range of points point that bear the origin, three axes, coordinate grid, and instrument installation fixed to frame. Even when time changes, the same placement positions are tracked, and exchange to distinct things that coincide at each time is not performed. It includes non-collinear directions that determine three-dimensional placement. The condition of stopping the motion of hands or gears inside a clock is not required.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: lengthinquiry
entries.meaning: inquiry takes as its subject the spatial length given by the closed relation of distance, using two points, a reference system, a calibrated length unit, and the correspondence of values. The length of an object is treated as the distance between the two endpoints determined according to the measurement method. The length of light's curved path, elapsed time, and string length are distinguished. Which endpoint event is chosen, the placement of the ruler, and the simultaneity condition for a moving rod are specified by each measurement method; this research subject's specification alone does not require actual measurement or agreement of all methods.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: timeinquiry
entries.meaning: inquiry takes as its subject the time assigned to events, systems, time units, and situations by assignment, and the time interval due to their difference and the time coincidence of simultaneity. The numerical values of time follow the rest clocks of each system, common reference, synchronization, and calibration, maintaining the validity and uniqueness of assignment according to the convention of the type of simultaneity. Non-assignment of readings or different origins are not supplemented as actual examples of physical time differences. Time itself is not identified with a clock as an object or a string of appellations, and the existence of specific events or actual measurement is not derived from this classification.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: frameinquiry
entries.meaning: For the quantity targeted in inquiry, the subject of research is how the judgment of values and agreement depends on the reference system and its measurement convention, while maintaining the correspondence of the same physical object and event and a calibrated scale. This is distinguished from mere unit conversion or name change and subjective preference. It does not state that values must always differ for all system pairs, directions, and cases; consistent special cases are allowed. This is a specification of the research domain and does not mean a proven specific transformation formula or conclusion.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: comparisonmoment
entries.meaning: The full range of time points of an interval with a time width that compares the motion of second relative to first. Numerical values are quantified using the same time convention of first, and excerpts to only endpoints, only measured samples, or only time points that appear uniform are not allowed. It permits multiple records representing time points to have the same time, while the validity of values and time width are separately required.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: motioncompleteness
entries.meaning: In the motion description of these two systems, scales, and context, eisk7 exhausts the full fixed placement of second, eisla exhausts the full time points of the comparison interval, and ym/yl correspond the placement and time with the same first scale, representing the completeness of range and correspondence. Points with different axis orientations and time points during acceleration are not omitted, and unknown ranges are not treated as complete. The availability of values, uniformity, and the holding of laws are not implied.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: commonvelocity
entries.meaning: The axis components of a velocity vector commonly tested for all placement points and all time points of second relative to the same first. The numerical values are expressed in lengthunit/timeunit, and the velocity is not reselected by taking a point or time point as an argument. They are candidate values allowing positive, negative, and zero, while the holding of constant velocity is separately required by displacement conditions.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: physicalsystem
entries.meaning: A system that physically describes a state and its change within the same context. It identifies the constituent parts of matter and fields, and physical quantities such as their positions, motions, electric quantities, field values, and objects of interaction, and fixes which range is followed as one system. It is not limited to rigid bodies or single particles or electrodynamics alone; it includes mechanics, fields, and light. The isolation of the system, equilibrium, invariance of state, and conformity to specific laws are not required.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: generallaw
entries.meaning: The full range of laws law that have general relations of physical quantities and application conditions governing state changes of physical systems within the same theory. The same content, with fixed correspondence of quantities, units, and objects, is applied to each coordinate system, without exchanging to another law for each system. It is not limited to only electrodynamics or optics, only successful laws, or only the literal agreement of formulas. The holding as a law in each system is separately given by eisbi, and the suitability of candidate descriptions is separately given by vi.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: generalhistory
entries.meaning: The complete candidate history of the physical system's state and its changes, in which the acceptability and unacceptability of each law of the same theory should be compared. The target system maintains correspondence between constituent parts, fields, physical quantities, and events. Do not restrict to only histories that actually occurred or conform to a law; include unchanged degenerate cases as candidates. vf connects to the same system, and vh connects to descriptions in each coordinate system of the same history.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: generallawcompleteness
entries.meaning: Completeness within the scope that all physical laws of the theory compared under this principle are eisle, all physical candidate histories are eislf, and vh exhausts all corresponding descriptions of the same history in each eligible system. Target both acceptable and unacceptable candidates, and do not allow preservation to hold by excluding inconsistent cases or cases where descriptions are missing on one side. Even certification that all laws can be finitely enumerated does not substitute for the truth of the laws.
context: Maintain the same task, method, object, document, and context. Distinguish appearance, possibility, adoption, and implementation.

entries.name: formulatesprinciple
entries.meaning: The author presents node's formulation as the formulation of a principle previously designated as an antecedent by designation in the same document. context: Completeness, actual existence, support of origin, and primitive relations are not back-calculated from results. Unknown inputs are not supplemented as false.

The five constituents of a value can be specialized to any eligible type under the same rule. The fact that infinite-type quantification can be described is separate from the fact that it can be computed by a finite executor.
